observation.description: Asset row attachment is impossible on packaged 0.1.7: ctx.assets.attach(assetId, { upload }) succeeds in the handler (host call runs, returns the canonical asset id — identical to the finalize-returned id), but EVERY subsequent write of that value into a v.assetRef field fails the commit with SNAPBACK_ASSET_REF_UNVERIFIED ('written without a ctx.assets.attach admission'). Isolated across four variants: restricted and unrestricted field forms, writing the attach return value and the raw input id, and a minimal single-write mutation whose only effect is the admitted insert. A mutation that calls attach and writes NO assetRef field commits fine, so the admission is registered but never visible to the commit validator. Consequences chained: the via-references sharing declaration is unreachable (delivery stays owner-only), and delete-refusal-while-referenced cannot be exercised. This is the arm's one check-level FAIL (A1-04).

competitorOutcome.description: The frozen Firebase Partiful arm attached Storage objects to rows as plain fields with rules-checked reads — no admission step to break. Snapback's admission design is stronger on paper (commit-boundary provenance) but currently blocks the entire attachment feature on the public closure.

mustNotRegress: Commit-boundary refusal of unadmitted assetRef writes, and attach's owner/intent validation (SNAPBACK_ASSET_ATTACH_DENIED / _INTENT_MISMATCH).
smallestCoherentFix: Make the transaction-scoped admission the host registers during ctx.assets.attach visible to the commit validator for the same invocation's buffered writes, with a packaged-closure conformance test that runs the guide's own createPhoto-shaped mutation end-to-end.
acceptanceWitness: The guide's attach snippet (insert with attachment: await ctx.assets.attach(...)) commits on a fresh external scaffold against the public closure, the reference edge appears, and delete-while-referenced refuses.
